summary: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU), part of Qatar Foundation in Doha, gives graduate scholarships made of tuition waivers and monthly stipends. Students are considered during admission and no separate application is needed. Waivers are 100% for PhD and 75% or 60% for most master's programmes, and the monthly stipend for international students is QAR 9,000 for PhD (45 months) and QAR 7,000 for Master's (21 months). Awards depend on funds and are not guaranteed.
eligibility_notes:
Awards are based on merit or financial need and depend on available funds; they are not automatically granted to admitted students. Applicants are considered during admission and need no separate scholarship application. Self-sponsored students are not eligible for waivers; they may get a discounted rate of QAR 2,000 per credit hour based on financial need. Students funded by an outside sponsor follow the sponsor's policy.

Stipends go to full-time graduate students who serve the university as a research assistant (RA) and/or teaching assistant (TA), subject to funds. Full-time working professionals, and part-time workers above 40% of full-time hours, are not eligible. Stipends do not depend on marital status or number of dependents.

Admission rules in most colleges: a bachelor's degree for master's programmes or a master's degree for PhD programmes, from a recognised university, with a GPA of at least 3.0 out of 4.0; a degree in a field the programme lists; IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 79 unless exempt; two recommendation letters (one academic); a personal statement; PhD applicants add a research proposal in several colleges. Research experience is preferred, especially for PhD. The College of Law asks for at least 3.0, preferring 3.3, for some LL.M. and S.J.D. routes. Scores must be no more than two years old in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. Requirements differ by college and programme, so read the college lists.

English exemptions: each college page sends applicants to the university admissions site for the exemption process. The older university policy (2018) lists exemption for applicants who studied in a country where English is the native language, who hold an official letter that English was the medium of instruction, or whose first language is English; the university may still ask for a test. College of Islamic Studies says no scholarships are available to international students in any graduate certificate programme. The School of Economics and Management says no waivers are offered for MS Economics. Applicants may submit up to two applications per academic year.
age_experience_notes: No age limit stated. Research experience is preferred, especially for PhD applicants (College of Science and Engineering and College of Health and Life Sciences). Health and medical applicants to the health management master's programmes in the College of Science and Engineering may be considered if they have programming knowledge and relevant work experience.
funding_summary: Tuition waivers: 100% for PhD (STEM and SHAPE) and S.J.D., 75% for STEM master's, 60% for SHAPE MS and MA and for J.D., 0% for LL.M., MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends for international students: QAR 9,000 per month (QAR 108,000 per year) for PhD for 45 months, and QAR 7,000 per month (QAR 84,000 per year) for Master's for 21 months. International students also get one round-trip airfare during candidature (inbound at start, outbound at graduation). Housing and meals are not paid separately. Scholarships are reviewed each year and renewal depends on academic progress and funds.
programmes_note: Programmes are offered by seven colleges and schools: College of Science and Engineering, College of Health and Life Sciences, College of Islamic Studies, College of Humanities and Social Sciences, College of Law, College of Public Policy, and School of Economics and Management. Waivers depend on the programme type (STEM, SHAPE, law, economics, certificate). The lists below show the programmes named on the college admission pages and the tuition page; the master's list is cut at 25. Not listed below: Master in Global Health Policy (College of Public Policy, 60% waiver), J.D. (60% waiver), LL.M. in International Economic and Business Law and LL.M. in International Law and Foreign Affairs (0% waiver), MSc in Economics (0% waiver, no waivers offered) and the graduate certificates (no waiver).
institutions_note: All programmes are at Hamad Bin Khalifa University, Doha, Qatar. Each college reviews applications for its own programmes. The 2018 admission policy says courses at HBKU are taught mostly in English, with two MA Islamic studies specialisations taught in Arabic.

benefits.limit_text: Waiver of 100% (PhD STEM, PhD SHAPE and S.J.D.), 75% (STEM MS), 60% (SHAPE MS and MA, J.D.), 0% (LL.M., MS Economics, certificates)
benefits.conditions: Tuition before waiver per credit hour: QAR 4,000 for STEM, QAR 2,500 for SHAPE, J.D. and MS Economics, QAR 2,000 for LL.M. and certificates. Self-sponsored students get no waivers. Reviewed annually; renewal depends on academic progress and funds.

benefits.limit_text: International PhD: QAR 9,000 per month (QAR 108,000 per year) for 45 months. International Master's: QAR 7,000 per month (QAR 84,000 per year) for 21 months.
benefits.conditions: Full-time students who serve as RA (10 hours per week with the primary supervisor) and/or TA (up to 10 hours per week at QAR 50 per hour in the semester assigned to teach); up to 10 additional paid hours per week through the Student Employment Program; the page also states a 20-hour weekly cap. Not for full-time working professionals or part-time workers above 40% of full-time hours. Depends on funds; stipend exceptions need dean and provost approval. Meals are not covered separately: the stipend is meant for general living costs.

benefits.limit_text: One round-trip airfare during candidature: an inbound ticket at programme start and an outbound ticket at graduation
Students pay their own housing, in Qatar Foundation dormitories or outside, from the stipend or personal funds

requirements.text: Completed online application form (create an account, choose college and programme). Up to two applications per academic year.

Official electronic transcripts submitted with the online application: final transcripts and graduation statements for all previous university study, with an explanation of the grading system; results from the last completed semester if studies are unfinished; official translation if not in English or Arabic. Applicants admitted on copies or incomplete transcripts must give originals at enrolment.

IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 79 (TOEFL institution code 4981; for IELTS ask the test centre to send the report to HBKU, no code). Official scores are sent directly to HBKU and copies uploaded with the application. College of Humanities and Social Sciences: scores no more than two years old. Exemptions are handled through the university admissions site.

GRE or GMAT scores (GRE code 7551, GMAT code H6S): required for PhD in Sustainable Energy and PhD in Sustainable Environment; optional for PhD in Computer Science and Engineering and PhD in Logistics and Supply Chain Management; not required for master's in the College of Science and Engineering. Also accepted for the Graduate Certificate in Islamic Psychology and Psychotherapy.
requirements.conditional_rule: Specific College of Science and Engineering PhD programmes

requirements.text: Two letters of recommendation, one from an academic referee (referee names and emails are entered after submitting; referees get an email request). Three letters for MS in Exercise Science and PhD in Biopsychology and Neuroscience (College of Health and Life Sciences).

Personal statement of 300 to 500 words (why you apply, how the programme supports your goals, research interests and achievements). Incomplete statements or ones below the minimum word count are not accepted (College of Science and Engineering). The College of Law and the School of Economics and Management describe a personal statement without a word count.

Research proposal using the college template: PhD in Humanities and Social Sciences 1,000 to 2,000 words, with four-year research plan; College of Islamic Studies 1,000 to 2,000 words, English and/or Arabic, not exceeding five pages, with a statement of language competence; College of Law LL.M. and S.J.D. 1,000 words. The College of Science and Engineering page does not mention one.
requirements.conditional_rule: PhD applicants in Humanities and Social Sciences and Islamic Studies; LL.M. and S.J.D. in Law

requirements.text: Writing sample of 15 to 20 pages, English and/or Arabic, academic in nature, with a key argument and proper citation.
requirements.conditional_rule: College of Islamic Studies programmes that list it

requirements.text: Current CV or resume covering academic qualifications, professional experience, publications, research projects, awards and conference presentations.
Electronic copy of passport. Qatari nationals and Qatar residents also submit a valid Qatari ID.
Non-refundable application fee of QAR 250. All documents must be PDF; materials not on the required list are discarded; submitted documents are not returned.

application_steps.title: Choose a college and programme and check its requirements
application_steps.detail: Read the admission requirements page of the college you want. International graduate applicants have until 01 Feb 2027 (the online graduate application opens on 01 Oct 2026); Qatari and resident applicants who want funding have until 15 Mar 2027. The pages do not say which intake term the 2027 round covers.

application_steps.title: Create an account and submit the online application
application_steps.detail: Register through the application system, log in, choose the college and programme and submit. You can submit up to two applications per academic year. Pay the non-refundable QAR 250 fee. There is no separate scholarship application: you are considered for scholarships during admission.

application_steps.title: Upload documents and give referee contact details
application_steps.detail: After submitting you get a confirmation email asking you to log in, upload the supporting documents as PDF files and enter your referees' contact details. Send official test scores to HBKU directly. Do not upload items that are not on the required list.

application_steps.title: Completeness check, college assessment and possible interview
application_steps.detail: The admissions team checks that the application is complete and that you are eligible, then sends it to the college for assessment. The 2018 admission policy says most applicants identified as very high potential are invited to an interview and very strong files may be admitted without one; the College of Humanities and Social Sciences page says scholarship awards follow an overall evaluation of documents and interviews.

application_steps.title: Decision and scholarship notification
application_steps.detail: Applicants are told when the college decides; accepted applicants receive an offer letter. Scholarships are decided on merit or need and depend on funds. Award notices are sent by email with the details of the award. The pages give no date for results.

application_steps.title: Accept the offer and finish enrolment
application_steps.detail: Per the 2018 admission policy, admitted students submit an enrolment form and pay a deposit or give a sponsor commitment letter, and send official test scores or a language waiver; the offer is valid only for the semester applied for, and a first-semester deferral of up to one semester needs approval. Check the current process with the college, as this policy is older.

application_steps.title: Do the assistant work and keep good academic standing
application_steps.detail: Stipend holders work as research assistant (10 hours per week with the supervisor) and/or teaching assistant. Scholarships are reviewed every year, and renewal depends on academic progress and available funds. Students must keep good academic standing as defined in the scholarship agreement; outside funding or deferring admission may affect eligibility.

The graduate admissions page lists only one named programme; the tuition page and college pages were used for the lists.
notes: Stored data carried over and re-confirmed: waivers 100% / 75% / 60% / 0%, stipends QAR 9,000 and QAR 7,000 with 45 and 21 months, airfare, housing not covered, deadline 01 Feb 2027, fee QAR 250, personal statement 300-500 words.

The scholarship page says the stipend cap is 20 hours a week in total and also lists RA 10 hours, TA up to 10 hours and Student Employment up to 10 hours; the page itself calls this unclear on how they combine.

The 2018 admission policy says standardized test scores are required for PhD programmes taught in English; the current College of Science and Engineering page makes GRE optional for some PhD programmes and required for others. The current college page is used.
